issues.legal_issue: A civil court may continue a validly instituted possession suit and its decree may be executed when a temporary exemption from rent-control protection expires while the suit is pending.
material_facts: The premises were newly constructed buildings that were exempt from the rent-control legislation for a fixed period after construction.
The landlords terminated the tenancies and filed possession suits while the buildings remained exempt.
The exemption period expired before the trial courts passed decrees for possession.
The decrees were upheld on appeal.
issues.conclusion: Expiry of the exemption during the pendency of the suits did not deprive the civil courts of jurisdiction to decide them, and the decrees for possession remained executable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 1(3) and 13(1) of the Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973, a suit validly instituted while a newly constructed building is exempt may proceed after the exemption expires. Section 13(1) does not expressly bar the civil court from deciding such a suit or prevent execution of its decree. The parties’ rights are determined by the law applicable when the suit is instituted; reading the Act otherwise would defeat the purpose of encouraging new construction and allow a tenant to frustrate that purpose by delaying litigation. The Court applied the reasoning in Firms Amar Nath Basheshar Dass v. Tek Chand, Shri Ram Saroop Rai v. Smt. Lilavati, Mohinder Kumar v. State of Haryana, Nand Kishore Marwah v. Samundri Devi, Atma Ram Mittal v. Ishwar Singh Punia, Kesho Ram & Co. v. Union of India, Suresh Chand v. Gulam Chisti, Ramesh Chandra v. III Additional District Judge, Bhola Nath Varshney v. Mulk Raj Madan, and Parripati Chandrasekharrao & Sons v. Alapati Jalaiah. It rejected the contrary approach in Vineet Kumar v. Mangal Sain Wadhera as no longer good law.

rule.if: civil_possession_suit and tenancy_terminated_before_filing and suit_filed_during_temporary_exemption and exemption_expired_before_decree

predicates.civil_possession_suit: A landlord brought a civil court proceeding seeking possession of rented premises.
predicates.tenancy_terminated_before_filing: The landlord terminated the tenancy before filing the possession suit.
predicates.suit_filed_during_temporary_exemption: The landlord filed the suit while the premises were within a temporary period of exemption from rent-control protection.
predicates.exemption_expired_before_decree: The temporary exemption expired before the court passed its decree.

issues.definition: When a landlord brings a civil possession suit after terminating the tenancy while the premises are temporarily exempt, and that exemption expires before judgment, the civil court may continue the suit and its decree remains executable.
